summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Mercantile Bank through Redwood Optimize quantization profiles with live examples and bench numbers. Discussion centered on INT8 for cost reduction, FP8 for better quality/latency balance, fallback policies, and metrics to validate. Customer requested benchmarks on their prompt set and SOC2/KMS notes for Private deployment. Agreed next steps: share spreadsheet, schedule 2-week POC, and provide quant-presets recommendations.

Private deployment considerations: KMS, VPC, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intro, I'm Ethan, AE at Redwood, and Priya our SE will drive most of the Optimize bits.
[00:08] Jared: Hi thanks, Jared here, head of ML at Mercantile Bank, Sonia and Ravi are on. We're mostly evaluating options to reduce inference cost while keeping compliance controls.
[00:18] Priya: Great, we'll focus today on quantization profiles in Redwood Optimize — INT8 and FP8 — and show quality vs latency comparisons and practical rollout patterns. Quick note, some auto transcript stuff may mis-spell FP8 as F P eight.
[00:32] Sonia: Sounds good. Our primary concerns: latency p95 < 300ms for customer-facing scoring, and < 1% quality regression vs our current fp16 baseline.
[00:45] Priya: Perfect, we'll show the typical deltas. First, quick primer: INT8 gives best token cost reduction but can introduce quality regressions for certain heads / long context scenarios; FP8 is kind of a middle ground — almost fp16-like quality for many models with ~20-40% cost savings and better latency in our runtime.
[01:10] Jared: Is FP8 supported across all models or only some families?
[01:15] Priya: Good question — support depends on model topology and whether the model was compiled with quant-friendly kernels. For our catalog we have verified FP8 on the 7B/13B families and many 30B variants; INT8 is broader but more sensitive to prompt distributions.
[01:32] Ethan: I'll also flag that Redwood Optimize will produce a quant-profile (a small artifact) showing per-layer sensitivity and recommended per-layer quantization.
[01:42] Sonia: Ok can you show some numbers?
[01:45] Priya: Sure, I'm sharing my screen — benchmark: baseline fp16 on a 13B model, tail p95 latency = 420ms, cost X; FP8 median latency = 280ms, p95 = 350ms, quality metric (BLEU/Rouge-ish) delta = -0.5% vs fp16; INT8 median = 220ms, p95 = 320ms, quality delta = -2.8% on our prompt suite. These are illustrative; your prompts matter a lot.
[02:25] Jared: So INT8 looks faster and cheaper but quality hit maybe too big for us. FP8 seems promising.
[02:31] Priya: Exactly, that's the common takeaway. Also note caching + batching interplay: with our continuous batching runtime, FP8's lower memory footprint improves batching and reduces p95 in practice.
[02:45] Ravi: From security: if we go Private or VPC, how does KMS and audit logging work for these quantized models?
[02:54] Priya: In Private deployments we keep the model artifacts inside the customer's environment; KMS/HSM integrations manage encryption at rest and key provisioning. Audit logs record inference calls (meta), and Redwood Console exposes per-model token-level usage. We'll send the SOC2 + KMS architecture note after the call.
[03:15] Sonia: If we wanted a staged rollout, can we do FP8 for low-risk routes and INT8 as a canary?
[03:22] Ethan: Yes — Redwood supports route-level model variants and automatic fallback. Typical pattern: default fp16 or fp8, canary INT8 for <5% traffic with quality monitoring; automatic rollback if evals dip beyond threshold.
[03:38] Priya: I'll show a config snippet — but quick caveat: INT8 often needs a per-customer eval set to tune per-layer clipping/scale factors; that's where Redwood Optimize profiles help.
[03:52] Jared: What metrics should we use to guard quality? We use a combination of business metrics and text-sim metrics.
[03:58] Priya: Right, Redwood recommends evaluate on your business prompts and track: 1) response accuracy (task-specific checks), 2) semantic similarity (embed-based), and 3) human-in-the-loop sampling for high-sensitivity cases. We provide eval harnesses and an eval runner that can produce a QC report.
[04:20] Sonia: Any chance the transcript picks up model names wrong — we've seen 'Redwood Optimize' mis-typed in docs before.
[04:26] Ethan: Ha, yes the transcript is rough sometimes.
[04:30] [05:00] Priya: Back to numbers — here's an example table (reading): fp16 cost baseline 1.0x / median 420ms / p95 520ms; FP8 0.65x cost / median 280ms / p95 350ms / quality -0.5%; INT8 0.45x cost / median 220ms / p95 320ms / quality -2.8%. Again these are model-and-prompt dependent.
[05:35] Jared: That -2.8% on INT8, is that on BLEU-like metric or downstream accuracy?
[05:40] Priya: That's on the surrogate quality metric in our bench (combination of ROUGE & semantic sim). In many retrieval-augmented or constrained generation tasks, INT8 regressions can be negligible. But for long-context summarization we've seen more sensitivity.
[05:58] Sonia: For our fraud-detection scoring, small hallucination regressions are unacceptable. So FP8 feels like the safer cut.
[06:07] Priya: Agree. FP8 commonly used in production as a speed/cost compromise. Another option is mixed quant: control-critical heads remain fp16 while others are quantized — Redwood Optimize can generate mixed profiles.
[06:22] Jared: How long to run a quant-profile on our 13B model with 5k prompts?
[06:29] Priya: For 5k prompts it can take a few hours on a dedicated cluster; Optimize supports streaming profiling — you don't need to profile the whole dataset at once. We'll run an initial pass then focus on high-sensitivity prompts.
[06:44] Ethan: We'll include a recommended bucketed prompt set in the spreadsheet to speed that up.
[06:49] [07:00] Priya: A couple of implementation notes: 1) kernel selection — our runtime picks kernels per layer to maximize throughput for INT8/FP8; 2) KV cache semantics — INT8 can increase cache miss sensitivity if quantization changes key distributions slightly, so we test KV-deduping; 3) telemetry — Redwood Console shows token-level latency and quality correlates over time.
[07:25] Ravi: On compliance, will audit logs still show token-level details if we keep them? We're restricted on PII.
[07:32] Priya: Logs are configurable — you can redact content and keep metadata only. For Private deployments logs never leave your VPC unless you opt-in.
[07:42] Sonia: Pricing impact? If FP8 is 0.65x and INT8 0.45x, how does that translate to our committed Dedicated price?
[07:50] Ethan: For Dedicated, unit price is tied to GPU hours and token throughput; FP8 reduces effective GPU time per token so you see similar multipliers as the cost numbers. We'll model your expected throughput and send a sample TCO spreadsheet.
[08:05] Jared: Great. One more technical: do we have automated rollback triggers based on evals, or is it manual?
[08:12] Priya: Both. You can set automated rollback thresholds in Redwood Console: if semantic-sim drops X% or latency exceeds Y ms, automations can route traffic back to baseline. We also support alerting and canary analysis reports.
[08:27] Sonia: Can we get sample configs for the canary A/B test?
[08:30] Priya: Yes, we'll attach sample routing and rollout YAML.
[08:35] [09:00] Jared: Ok next steps then?
[09:04] Ethan: Action summary: we'll send the benchmark spreadsheet and quant-presets, Priya will prepare the per-layer recommendations, and you (Jared) will send a prompt set. We'll propose a POC start date once we have the prompts.
[09:18] Jared: Sounds good, aiming to get prompts to you by 2026-04-20.
[09:24] Ethan: Great, we'll target a 2-week POC with FP8 baseline + INT8 canary.
[09:30] Priya: Anything else on security or deployment?
[09:33] Ravi: Please include SOC2 scope and KMS keyflow diagrams.
[09:36] Ethan: Will do.
[09:40] [09:50] Priya: Alright I'll stop share, Ethan will send the links. Thanks everyone.
[09:55] Jared: Thanks both.
[10:00] Meeting end.

Note: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings and shorthand; timestamps approximate.
